subject: Sorry Rofer...
author: Segaswirl
body:
But to me Revenge isn't much better than Paradise... it's probably the sloppiest and laziest game in the whole series, nowhere near as refined as Burnout 2 and 3. Both Paradise and Revenge are still good games though... in their own way. Revenge for it's sense of speed and umm... errr, verticles? The 360 exclusive freezing feature is also nice. Paradise for it's good looks and it's attempt to be a more social game (even though that's not really my thing as I prefer hardcore mute racing :p, but it's a quality the game has whether I like it or not).

Criterion have said themselves that they want to do something different with Burnout each time they put a game in the series out... and that's fine, but they can't seriously expect every fan to go along with them when they do something as... unique... as Paradise. Having said that I do hope they keep the servers running for a long time when it comes to whatever older game in the series people like best.

Oh and Rofer, once again... B3 >>> Revenge (even when racing in compacts). 😛

subject: dnekcoc.
author: kevlar0
body:
So Rofer, you don't think Paradise is a burnout game?, i was playing with hawkeye on Paradise yesterday for a couple of hours we did the bikes for a while then we did a bit of racing and stuff, and yes he whined and moaned about pretty much everything but he did get into the swing of things, trying to beat roadtimes and getting a couple of decent results in ranked racing (he got his rank down to about 10000 which ain't too shabby for a greenhorn), in the end he buggered off back on Revenge for a few races to get his confidence back (although i did see him playing single player later on trying to get the revenge racer lol).

His main complaint was that he didn't get all the cars without having to put some effort in, Unlike Revenge where ALL the cars were giftwrapped on a silver platter and given to even the greenest of noob, which is great, but there is only 1 car in revenge (no its not the 190 Nito, you have mad elite skillz and we are not worthy), so there is no real need to complete the offline game.

Paradise on the other hand, nothing is given to you, you have to earn it by playing the offline and this is what makes Paradise a Burnout game, you do get the old Burnout feel playing it offline and you do get a sense of achievment for unlocking the faster cars later on in the game which you can use online.

In my opinion if you are too lazy to unlock some of the faster vehicles on paradise you will never see the full potential online, and will probably be driving around in the hunter calvery when they sunsettle the revenge servers next year, good luck with that dude.

He's not the messiah, he's a very naughty boy.

subject: OCD
author: kevlar0
body:
About 90% of my friends list is made up from people I have met whilst playing the Burnout series, some from B3 some from Revenge and some from Paradise, this being said I consider each and everyone one of them to be a “true” burner along with all the people on this site.

Its not the amount you play or the game mode you favor, hell, some of the old school burners from B3 didn’t get on with revenge so have pretty much stopped playing Burnout altogether but I still consider them true burners.

Whether you crash, race, flatspin, glen, go for road times or whatever floats your boat, we all have one thing in common (apart from being monobrowed knuckle draggers), the adrenaline rush we get every time we play, be it from taking down a rival to hitting all the vehicles on a crash junction, even glenning a fast lap must give you a buzz (for the record I have never glenned a lap because I don’t know how to, as my lap times show),

What I see When I’m playing on FPS games with Burners is the run and gun attitude, fast and aggressive straight in, all guns blazing just like the start of a race, kill them before they kill you kinda attitude, whereas people I have met from playing FPS games are much more measured and tactical (boring camping srekcuf) they don’t tend to die as much, but they spend 10 minutes behind a wall waiting for an idiot like me to come into sight so they can pop a cap in my arse ( I iz Street bro innit).

Its hard to put ones finger on any one aspect of burnout that make one a “true burner”, for me its many things, only because I am a fan of all the Burnout titles that have been released and all for different reasons, all I know is that its like drug and I need a fix pretty much everyday.

And hn6 please let me have at least one road rule time you obsessive compulsive dratsab, have you taken uphill yet?? I did it in the carbon uber btw.

He's not the messiah, he's a very naughty boy.
